speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You presented with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation; can you describe exactly how your mental state has changed, such as confusion, lethargy, or agitation?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your history of tics and use of haloperidol, could you describe exactly what the "altered mentation" feels like—is it confusion, drowsiness, or something else? Also, have you noticed any involuntary muscle movements (dystonia or dyskinesia) in your neck, face, or tongue since starting the medication?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS).

The combination of fever, altered mentation, generalized rigidity, and profuse sweating in a patient on haloperidol is highly characteristic of NMS. I will now request a Creatine Kinase (CK) level to confirm muscle breakdown associated with this condition.
